title: Non-blocking follow-ups from backend-trade-journal-entry-notes review (PR #213)
description: Non-blocking findings from the pr-reviewer pass on PR #213 (free-text entry_notes on positions/closed trades), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's convention so they aren't lost once the PR merges.

checklist.step: PositionIn.entry_notes has no field_validator to strip whitespace or normalize an empty string to null, unlike PositionIn.ticker's `_strip_and_require_non_blank_ticker`. Today an explicit `entry_notes: ""` is stored/returned as `""` rather than `null`, and a whitespace-only note (e.g. `"   "`) is truthy under `if position.entry_notes:` in add_position's merge branch, so it would still get appended onto an existing note. Decide whether entry_notes should strip/normalize to null the same way ticker does, or whether free-text notes are deliberately exempt from that normalization, and record the decision either way.

decisions.decision: Added `PositionIn._strip_and_normalize_entry_notes`, a field_validator on `entry_notes` that strips leading/trailing whitespace and normalizes a resulting empty string to `None` (rather than storing/returning `""`, and rather than leaving free-text notes exempt from normalization entirely). This mirrors `PositionIn.ticker`'s own strip convention, but normalizes instead of rejecting: unlike `ticker` (required, `min_length=1`) or `FollowUpReviewIn.follow_up_notes` (required, whose entire purpose is recording the note, so a blank one would defeat the endpoint), `entry_notes` is optional -- an explicit blank/whitespace-only value has no meaningful difference from simply omitting the field, so silently normalizing to null (matching the already-omitted case) is more useful than a 422 that would force the caller to strip client-side or an inconsistent `""` vs `null` distinction leaking through the API. This also fixes the merge-append bug for free: `add_position`'s `if position.entry_notes:` check now correctly treats a whitespace-only incoming note as falsy (it's already `None` by the time the handler runs), so it's no longer appended onto an existing note as literal whitespace.
decisions.rationale: Considered leaving entry_notes deliberately exempt from normalization (i.e. treating the truthy-whitespace merge quirk as an accepted edge case) since the original backend-trade-journal-entry-notes task didn't flag it as a requirement -- rejected because it's a real, user-visible inconsistency (ticker normalizes, entry_notes silently doesn't) with no offsetting benefit: nothing in docs/Analyse.md or docs/ideas.md's ch. 59 entry calls for preserving whitespace-only notes, and the inconsistency was exactly what PR #213's review flagged. Considered rejecting a blank/whitespace-only entry_notes with a 422 (mirroring ticker/follow_up_notes) instead of normalizing -- rejected because entry_notes is optional and free-text: a caller who sends `entry_notes: ""` almost certainly means 'no note', not an error condition, and forcing a 422 here would be surprising for an optional field in a way it isn't for a required one like follow_up_notes.

review.notes: Verified the task-worker's claims directly rather than trusting the merge-branch comment. Instantiated PositionIn directly with '   ', '', '  hello  ', None for entry_notes -- got None, None, 'hello', None, exactly as claimed. Traced add_position's code path: `position` is the already Pydantic-validated PositionIn instance by the time the handler runs, so the field_validator's normalization has already happened before `if position.entry_notes:` in the merge branch evaluates it -- the merge-append bug fix is real, not just documented. Confirmed the existing non-blank merge-append test (test_merge_with_incoming_notes_appends_to_existing_notes) still passes, so normal append behavior is unaffected. Diffed backend/openapi.json and frontend/src/api/types.ts against main: description-string-only, no shape change. Full suites green: backend pytest --cov=app 1134 passed/99.95% coverage, frontend vitest --coverage 704 passed/~99.7% coverage; ruff/mypy/eslint/tsc all clean; scripts/check_profit_target_wording.py and scripts/validate_tasks.py clean. Ran the code-review skill (background) independently, which corroborated: no correctness bugs, no removed guards/broken call sites, no CLAUDE.md violations. No frontend consumer of entry_notes exists yet (only present in generated types.ts), so no UI surface to walk through -- browser walkthrough and e2e run explicitly skipped on that basis. Checklist's 'decide X' item has a substantive corresponding decisions entry. No blocking or non-blocking findings; no followups task filed.
